docs.summary: When above zero, every frame advances time by exactly this many seconds instead of the measured time, so a run plays out the same way every time, for reference captures and recordings.

How far the frame being drawn sits past the last fixed step, in seconds - the fixed loop leaves this holding whatever part of the frame its steps did not consume, so it is always under [`FixedDeltaTime`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Time~FixedDeltaTime) by the time the scene's Update runs. This is the alpha physics interpolation has to render at. Counting time since the last step with a per-frame accumulator instead does not work: the step that resets such a counter happens partway through a frame, and the whole of that frame's delta then gets added on top of time the step already consumed, which reads back a pose the body has not reached yet. Owned by the game loop - read it, do not write it.
How far drawing is from the last fixed step toward the next, 0 to 1.

docs.summary: The base time scale. Time runs at [`EffectiveTimeScale`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Time~EffectiveTimeScale), this times every active modifier.
The scale time actually runs at: [`TimeScale`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Time~TimeScale) times every active [`TimeScaleModifier`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.TimeScaleModifier).

Multiplies the time scale until the returned modifier is removed. Use this rather than setting [`TimeScale`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Time~TimeScale) for temporary effects (slow motion, hit stop), since several can overlap and each removes only its own. Modifiers belong to the current time context, so play mode's end with it.
